subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): generic outbound delivery-report seam; WhatsApp native auto-reply reports provider-accepted sends

question: Should OpenClaw accept openclaw/plugin-sdk/outbound-delivery-report as the public contract for plugin self-delivered outbound sends once real WhatsApp/runtime proof is attached?
rationale: This is a new public Plugin SDK seam with release-facing naming and idempotency semantics, so automation should not decide the permanent API contract from tests alone.

options.title: Accept seam after proof
options.body: Require redacted WhatsApp/runtime proof and explicit maintainer acceptance of the name, input shape, idempotency scope, and session-key behavior before merge.

options.title: Redesign the SDK contract
options.body: Keep the linked issue open and ask for a narrower or differently named contract before adding a public subpath.

options.title: Pause this PR
options.body: Do not merge the branch until maintainers settle whether outbound hook parity should use a generic report seam or a broader core observer design.

recommendation.title: Accept seam after proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted WhatsApp/runtime proof and explicit maintainer acceptance of the name, input shape, idempotency scope, and session-key behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged and co-authored adjacent outbound hook contract work and is the strongest routing signal for the cross-boundary API decision.
